title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (Consolidated handbook)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This consolidated handbook page provides a single reference for working at Redwood, our role and career ladder framework, core benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools every Redwooder needs to know. It is intended for new hires, hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineers who onboard teammates. For detailed policy or legal text, see the linked pages in Related pages.

Scope

- Audience: all Redwood employees and contractors.
- Purpose: unify the common operational guidance used during hiring, onboarding, and career development.
- Owner: People Operations (people-ops).
- Review cadence: annual by People Ops with role-matched reviewers; immediate updates for significant policy changes.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Overview
Redwood is an engineering-first company building inference infrastructure. We value ownership, clarity, and pragmatic decision-making. Everyone is expected to:

- Ship high-quality work and iterate quickly.
- Communicate asynchronously in Slack and Confluence with clear context.
- Use data and metrics to inform trade-offs (latency, cost, correctness).
- Be inclusive: treat teammates with respect and advocate for diverse perspectives.

Core working norms

- Async-first: reduce unnecessary meetings; use Confluence for decisions and ADRs.
- Open collaboration: encourage cross-team reviews and pair design sessions.
- Blameless postmortems: focus on learning and systemic fixes after incidents.

Performance and feedback

- Managers run quarterly check-ins and an annual performance review. Goals are set using OKRs and role-level success criteria (see Roles & Career Ladders).
- Continuous feedback is encouraged: use 1:1s for growth conversations and Slack for quick kudos or clarifying feedback.

2) Roles & career ladders (high level)

Principles

- Ladders are competency-based, not solely tenure-based. Promotions require demonstrated impact, ownership, and leadership relative to the role level.
- Each functional ladder specifies expectations across three dimensions: Craft (execution quality), Scope (breadth of impact), and Leadership (influence and mentorship).

Typical ladders at Redwood

- Individual Contributor engineering: IC1, IC2, IC3, Senior IC (IC4), Staff, Principal.
- Engineering management: EM1 (first-line manager), EM2 (manager of managers), Director.
- Product: PM1, PM2, Senior PM, Group PM.
- Cross-functional ladders: Design, SRE, DevRel, Research/Applied ML.

Promotion indicators (example checklist for IC2 -> IC3)

1. Consistent delivery of non-trivial projects (3+ month scope).
2. High code quality and system design that meets performance and reliability SLOs.
3. Mentorship of more junior engineers and active participation in design reviews.
4. Clear communication with peers, product, and support teams.

Documentation and artifacts

- Every promotion packet includes: summary of impact, 3–5 concrete examples, manager endorsement, and at least two peer references.
- People Ops maintains the master ladder matrices and sample promotion narratives.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health and financial

- Medical, dental, and vision plans with company-subsidized premiums.
- Flexible HSA and FSA contributions.
- 401(k) with company match for eligible employees.

Time off and flexible work

- Generous vacation policy (discussed with manager; manager approval required for planned absences).
- Company-observed holidays and an annual 5-day winter office closure.
- Flexible remote-first policy with optional office days for team syncs and onboarding.

Family and wellbeing

- Parental leave: primary caregiver: 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver: 6 weeks paid.
- Mental health benefits including counseling sessions and wellness stipend.

Career and learning

- Training and conference allowance per employee annually.
- Learning days for internal hackathons, knowledge-sharing, and conference attendance.

Perks and allowances

- Hardware stipend for home office, relocation support for new hires, commuter benefits where applicable, and catered team events for in-person weeks.

How to find full plan details

- Benefits summaries, plan documents, and vendor links live on the People Ops benefits portal and the Finance benefits page (internal links). Contact benefits@redwood.com for policy clarifications.

4) Hiring journey and onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy

- We hire for mission-alignment, technical excellence, and culture add. Interview loops are designed to evaluate role-specific skills and collaboration.
- Redwood is committed to equitable hiring: inclusive job descriptions, structured interviews, and calibrated feedback.

Typical interview process (engineer)

1. Recruiter screen: role fit, compensation band, candidate questions.
2. Technical screen: take-home or live coding (role-dependent).
3. Onsite loop: 4–6 interviews including system design, implementation, domain-specific (ML/inference) questions, and cross-functional partner interviews.
4. Hiring committee review and offer approval.

Decision criteria and timelines

- Target time-to-offer: 2–3 weeks from first screen for standard roles.
- Interviewers score consistently using a rubric that maps to ladder expectations.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)

Week 0 (pre-start)
- HR sends offer packet, hardware and workstation survey, and first-day schedule.
- Manager assigns a buddy and creates a 30-60-90 day plan template.

Week 1
- Orientation: People Ops welcome session, security training, benefits overview.
- Team onboarding: meet team, set up dev environment, walkthrough architecture and core repos.

Month 1
- Deliver a small scoped task with code review and ship it to staging.
- Regular 1:1 meetings with manager and buddy check-ins weekly.

Month 2–3
- Own a well-scoped project that contributes to team OKRs.
- Clear performance feedback checkpoint at 90 days.

Onboarding owner matrix (high level)

- People Ops: orientation, benefits, policy.
- Hiring manager: role onboarding, 30-60-90 plan, performance expectations.
- Buddy: day-to-day support and tribal knowledge.
- Eng Dev team/mentor: technical ramp and codebase familiarity.

5) Internal tools guide (essential tools & first actions)

Core tools and purpose

- Slack: asynchronous & synchronous communication. Join #announcements, #engineering, team channels, and your cohort channel.
- Confluence: canonical documentation and ADRs. Add or update pages when you make decisions.
- Git (GitHub Enterprise): repositories for services and infra. Follow repository CONTRIBUTING.md and code review guidelines.
- Jira (or Asana): work tracking — create tasks, link PRs to issues, and use sprint boards where applicable.
- Okta: single sign-on for company apps. Provisioning handled by IT.
- GCP/AWS console: cloud accounts for builds, logs, and metrics; access granted through role-based policies.

First-day checklist for tools

1. Confirm SSO (Okta) access and enable MFA.
2. Join Slack and set a profile with working hours and preferred pronouns.
3. Complete Confluence orientation and find your team-space pages.
4. Clone core repos and run the local dev environment onboarding script: ./dev/setup.sh (see README).

Access & security

- All tool access is granted by role and team. Request additional permissions via the internal access portal (link in Confluence).
- Secrets: store secrets in the authorized vault (KMS/HSM-backed); do not commit credentials to Git.

6) Manager and hiring manager checklist (operational)

Hiring managers should:
- Create an inclusive job spec using People Ops templates.
- Assemble diverse interview panels and use structured rubrics.
- Provide timely feedback and close loops with candidates.

First 30 days manager checklist for new hires:

- Week 0: prepare onboarding plan and hardware.
- Week 1: host orientation and set immediate goals.
- Week 2–4: ensure small-scope deliverable and technical ramp.

7) Career growth programs and mentoring

- Mentorship program pairs new hires with a technical mentor for 3–6 months.
- Internal mobility: employees may apply for open roles after 6 months with manager approval.
- Career workshops: promotion narrative clinics and manager calibration sessions run quarterly.

8) Policies & escalation (high level)

- Code of Conduct: expected behavior, reporting channels, and investigation process.
- Escalation: people-ops handles HR matters; engineering SRE/Platform on-call handles operational incidents per runbooks.

9) FAQs (selected)

Q: What if I need time off for caregiving?
A: Contact People Ops for leave options; parental and caregiving leaves are supported and may be paid depending on role/tier.

Q: How do I request an internal transfer?
A: Discuss with your manager and file an internal mobility request via the careers portal; transfers generally require manager approvals and a six-month tenure recommendation.

Q: Where are performance ladders stored?
A: The canonical ladder matrix and example narratives live in People Ops Ladders space in Confluence (linked in Related pages).

10) Links and references

- People Ops benefits portal (internal link).
- Engineering ladders and promotion guidance (internal link).
- Security & access request portal.
- IT hardware and vendor procurement docs.

Appendix: simple role-level matrix (text table)

Level | Typical years | Scope | Example expectations
IC1 | 0–2 | Task-level | Implements features with guidance, writes tests.
IC2 | 1–3 | Component-level | Owns components, participates in designs, mentors interns.
IC3 | 3–6 | System-level | Designs services, improves performance and reliability.
Senior / IC4 | 5+ | Cross-team | Leads major projects, influences architecture.

Contacts and escalation paths

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits questions: benefits@redwood.com
- IT & hardware requests: it-requests@redwood.com
- Security incidents: security@redwood.com (follow incident reporting runbook)

Change log

- 2023-11-01: Document created (initial consolidated draft).
- 2024-06-15: Updated parental leave and onboarding checklist.
- 2026-02-01: Annual review and updated internal tools checklist and promotion packet requirements.

If you have edits or suggestions, please open a PR against this page or contact People Ops.
